apod.explanation: A crescent Moon and bright Venus appear together over Poland's Tatra Mountains at dusk in a planetary conjunction, with the bright star Spica — a triple star system about 250 light-years away in Virgo — just to Venus's left.
apod.title: Moon, Venus and Spica Meet

breaking.fact: Explosions were heard across Kyiv early Thursday and Moscow said it shot down five drones, hours after Abu Dhabi talks ended with a prisoner exchange agreed but no ceasefire; Kushner and Witkoff meet Putin on Thursday, then Zelenskyy in Dublin.
breaking.headline: Kyiv and Moscow hit in overnight strikes as US envoys head to Moscow

breaking.fact: A cross-country storm system reaches Texas this weekend, triggering a level 1-of-4 flash-flood threat for Houston, San Antonio and Corpus Christi, with rain likely Sunday; parts of Texas have already had one of their wettest Novembers on record.
breaking.headline: Weekend storm to bring flash-flood threat to Houston

items.body: The Liberian-flagged VLCC Fujairah Energy was hit by a projectile on Nov 10 while sailing Al Ruwais to Dubai; four of 22 crew were injured. It is at least the eighth Sinokor tanker attacked in Hormuz since July; the IMO counts 133 confirmed incidents and 25 seafarer deaths as of Nov 10.
items.headline: Projectile strike on Sinokor VLCC Fujairah Energy injures four crew

items.body: UKMTO issued Warning 202-26 on Nov 11 after a report concerning a tanker in the strait; India's shipping minister identified the vessel as the Saudi-flagged NCC Fajr and said the whole crew was safe, including three Indian nationals. No damage or weapon has been confirmed.
items.headline: Second tanker incident in two days: Saudi-flagged NCC Fajr in possible attack

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Wednesday's rebound held into the close: S&P 500 +1.31% to 7,619.38, Nasdaq +1.60% to 25,466.19, Dow +0.49% to 52,486.49 as CoreWeave (+25%) revives the AI trade. Overnight, futures slipped — S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq about -0.9% — as Nvidia plunged ~8.6% after hours on reports its board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang; no decision has been announced. Oil settled higher (WTI $86.53, Brent $92.76) on Hormuz attack risk, then eased overnight; the VIX fell to 17.49. The bond market was closed for Veterans Day, so the 10-year yield is Tuesday's 4.98%.

space.body: NASA opened applications Nov 7 for its 25th astronaut class, the first since 2024; the deadline is Dec 3, 2026, with selection late 2027 and training from early 2028. With only 32 active astronauts on the books, the new class will train for the Moon, the planned Moon Base and Mars prep — at Johnson Space Center in Houston.
space.headline: NASA opens applications for its next astronaut class — first in two years

space.body: Astronomers found an invisible object of about 2.2 solar masses tugging on a red giant in binary system J0008+0128 — most likely a neutron star far heavier than the usual 1.4 solar masses, a puzzle for how such objects form. The finding is published in Science Advances.
space.headline: Possible supermassive neutron star found hiding beside a red giant

space.body: HKUST researchers found the deep-sea mollusk Chaetoderma shenloong evolved a previously unknown organelle, the ‘dracosphera’ — a 10–15 µm sphere wrapped in 20+ membrane layers housing hundreds to thousands of sulfur-oxidizing bacteria — letting it survive in near-oxygen-free cold-seep sediment. The work is published in Nature Communications.
space.headline: Deep-sea mollusk evolved a brand-new organelle — tiny ‘dragon balls’ housing bacteria

weekInBrief.body: October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (forecast +0.3%) and core +0.3%, but the BLS published no year-over-year rate because October 2025 prices were never collected during the 2025 shutdown. December hike odds moved to ~100%, and the 2-year Treasury yield jumped 18.9bp to 4.736%.
weekInBrief.headline: October CPI came in hot — and for the first time ever, there's no annual rate

weekInBrief.body: All 101 economists polled expect a December hike to 4.00–4.25%, and 55% say it ends the cycle; the same poll has PCE inflation not returning to 2% until at least 2028.
weekInBrief.headline: Reuters poll: Fed to raise rates once more in December

weekInBrief.body: Brent rose to $92.76 (+1.39%) and WTI to $86.53 (+0.57%) at the Nov 11 close, recovering from two-month lows; 37 vessels were attacked in and around Hormuz in October — the highest monthly tally of the war — and 10 more so far in November.
weekInBrief.headline: Oil rebounds from two-month lows as Hormuz attacks dent truce hopes

weekInBrief.body: After meeting Qatar's PM, Trump said the conflict was moving toward an end ‘fairly soon’ and further US strikes were ‘quite unlikely,’ with forces remaining ready and the naval blockade of Iran staying in place for now; Iran says Hormuz stays closed until its conditions are met.
weekInBrief.headline: Trump says Iran war winding down ‘fairly soon,’ but the naval blockade stays
